mission: Forensic investigation of (1) the development sanity stall and (2) the ARCH_PIPELINE truncation-metadata asymmetry. No held-out task touched. No production modified, paused, or reconfigured.

which_candidates: task_11 (strip_leading_prose), ARCH_PIPELINE, model=qwen2.5-coder:7b (the pinned model, confirmed correctly propagated), generation_time=208.16s, correctly classified TASK_LOGIC_FAILURE (a genuine, real logic bug in the generated regex, not an artifact)

task_11 (strip_leading_prose), ARCH_COUNCIL, model_used=council_synthesis, 4 real calls, generation_time=451.2s, PASSED, classification=PASS -- a real, live demonstration that on this exact task, the council mechanism succeeded where the pipeline mechanism failed. This is n=1, development-task data; per this investigation's own scope, NO capability conclusion is drawn from it -- it is recorded here purely as evidence the apparatus can and does produce real, complete, differentiated results across arms when given enough time.

This is the central piece of evidence separating 'apparatus is invalid' from 'apparatus is valid but starved.'

part1_development_sanity_diagnosis.is_the_harness_process_alive_or_deadlock: ALIVE, not deadlocked -- confirmed by real, if slow, wall-clock progress (one full candidate completed; CPU time on the harness process itself crept upward across repeated checks, consistent with genuine I/O-wait on a queued request, not a hang) and by ollama ps showing continuous, active model residency (not an idle/crashed Ollama server)
part1_development_sanity_diagnosis.is_one_arm_disproportionately_affected: cannot yet be fully determined at n=1 completed candidate -- but ARCH_COUNCIL (the arm currently stalled, per the recorded arm order) requires 4 real sequential calls versus ARCH_PIPELINE's 1, meaning it structurally has 4x the exposure to being queued behind concurrent production traffic for the SAME task, independent of any inherent difficulty
part1_development_sanity_diagnosis.internal_harness_sequencing_problem_rule: the harness's own sequencing is confirmed correct (task -> randomized arm order -> per-arm generation -> verification -> next arm) via the code-level verification already completed in the prior mission; the delay is external (real Ollama queue contention), not an internal loop/logic defect, based on direct correlation with concurrent production log activity

part1_classification.verdict: A and C together, not B. The apparatus is technically valid (proven by the one real, correctly-classified candidate) but cannot obtain a clean, timely measurement environment while at least three live production autonomous loops compete for the same single-threaded Ollama queue. This is documented as an EXPERIMENTAL PREREQUISITE, not worked around: 'the Tier-3 experiment (including its own development sanity check) requires either an explicit low/no-contention window, or acceptance of substantially longer, patient, unattended wall-clock time per candidate under real production load.'

critical_additional_finding_not_explicit.title: classify_result()'s ground-truth lookup is NOT scoped per-call -- a REAL, CONFIRMED cross-arm event-contamination bug
critical_additional_finding_not_explicit.mechanism: _truncation_events is a single, shared, global, time-windowed (300s) list. classify_result() takes recent[-1] -- the MOST RECENTLY APPENDED event within the window -- with no check that this event actually corresponds to the call currently being classified.
critical_additional_finding_not_explicit.why_this_is_safe_for_BASE_1_BASE_N_and_A: each of these arms' own generation call is the LAST thing appended to _truncation_events immediately before that arm's own classify_result() runs (sequential, non-concurrent execution within one process) -- so recent[-1] is correctly their own event, by construction of the execution order, not by any explicit scoping in the code.
critical_additional_finding_not_explicit.why_this_is_a_real_bug_specifically_for_: ARCH_PIPELINE's own call path NEVER appends anything to _truncation_events (confirmed in Part II -- its underlying call bypasses the shared capture point entirely). This means whenever classify_result() runs for an ARCH_PIPELINE candidate, recent[-1] -- IF non-empty -- is ALWAYS some OTHER arm's leftover event, never its own, because it has none to contribute.
critical_additional_finding_not_explicit.synthetic_proof: a direct unit test constructed a Pipeline-shaped call (a normal, valid-looking, closed-fence response that failed verification for an ordinary reason) with a stale done_reason='length' event from a DIFFERENT, unrelated arm sitting in the shared list from 5 seconds earlier. Result: WRONGLY classified GENERATION_TRUNCATED. Confirmed live via direct test execution, not asserted.
critical_additional_finding_not_explicit.why_the_one_real_completed_candidate_was: task_11's recorded arm order was [ARCH_PIPELINE, ARCH_COUNCIL, BASE_N, BASE_1] -- ARCH_PIPELINE ran FIRST, before any stream_query_ollama-routed call had populated _truncation_events at all, so recent was correctly empty and the fence-heuristic (correctly) decided the outcome. This was fortunate ordering, not a property of correct code -- a different randomized order, or a second task, could readily have produced the contaminated result.
critical_additional_finding_not_explicit.severity: real, confirmed, and MORE consequential than the originally-disclosed 'Pipeline lacks its own signal' gap alone -- that gap is an ABSENCE of information (leading at worst to under-detection, correctly falling back to the fence heuristic); this bug is a FALSE-ATTRIBUTION risk (leading to a wrong classification using a real signal that belongs to a different call entirely).

part3_truncation_bias_analysis.does_pipeline_systematically_bias_the_pr: YES, a real, confirmed risk exists -- but it is CONDITIONAL, not universal: it manifests specifically when an ARCH_PIPELINE candidate is classified within 300 seconds of ANY other arm's call that itself hit done_reason='length', regardless of task or arm identity. Given this investigation's own repeatedly-measured real generation times (tens of seconds to several minutes per call, frequently under heavy contention), a 300-second window is not a rare or edge-case gap -- it is comparable to or shorter than typical real inter-call spacing observed this session, making this a live, practically-relevant risk, not a theoretical one.

part3_conclusion: CONCLUSION B — measurement asymmetry is a real blocker, but the specific mechanism found is BROADER and MORE SERIOUS than the originally-scoped 'Pipeline lacks done_reason' concern: it is a scoping bug in the harness's own shared-state tracking, not merely a production-code limitation. This must be repaired (design only, not implemented per this mission's own instruction) before any held-out data collection.

part3_minimum_repair_design_not_implemen.proposed_change: Tag every _truncation_events entry, at capture time, with a unique per-call identifier (e.g. a monotonically-incrementing call counter, or a (task_id, arm, call_index) tuple set as a thread-local/module-level 'current call' marker immediately before each generation call and cleared immediately after). classify_result() must then look up ONLY the event whose tag matches the CURRENT call's own marker -- never 'the most recent event regardless of source'. For ARCH_PIPELINE specifically, since its call path structurally cannot ever produce a tagged event (confirmed in Part II), classify_result() should EXPLICITLY branch on a known arm-capability flag ('this arm has no ground-truth truncation signal') and skip the ground-truth lookup entirely for it, falling through cleanly to the fence heuristic every time -- rather than silently querying a list that could contain irrelevant data.
part3_minimum_repair_design_not_implemen.why_this_is_the_minimum_repair: does not touch any production file (self_edit_manager.py, river_deliberation.py, ollama_handler.py, echo_model_orchestrator.py all remain untouched); does not add retries; does not make F1 influential; does not change the primary endpoint (PASS/FAIL still comes from real sandboxed execution); does not give any arm additional inference opportunity -- it only corrects which piece of already-captured metadata gets consulted for which call.
part3_minimum_repair_design_not_implemen.not_implemented_per_explicit_instruction: STOPPED here, as instructed. This design is reported for review, not applied.

part4_reassessment.2_is_basen_genuinely_budget_matched: Structurally yes (2 call sites, N=3+1=4 total, max_tokens=2048 explicit throughout, temperature via the real, reused _jittered_temperature() function) -- but this remains STRUCTURALLY verified only; zero real BASE_N candidates have completed in this session, so its REAL total generated-token/wall-clock behavior against a live model remains unobserved. Council's own real per-councillor+synthesis budget is identical in call-count and max_tokens by design; model identity is intentionally different (pinned single model vs. real diverse pool) per the diversity-vs-compute question this comparison exists to ask.
part4_reassessment.3_is_the_synthesis_comparison_still_defe: Defensible in structure, genuinely uncertain in effect, exactly as it should be reported rather than assumed. The two templates differ in more than trivial wording (19 vs 29 lines) -- it is NOT established, and this investigation does not claim, that this makes synthesis 'equally easy' for both arms. A prompt instructing a model to reconcile its OWN near-identical attempts (BASE_N) is plausibly an EASIER synthesis task than reconciling genuinely divergent, differently-styled outputs from different real models (ARCH_COUNCIL) -- OR plausibly a HARDER one, if a model finds it harder to manufacture genuine self-critique of its own output than to arbitrate between visibly different ones. Both directions are plausible; neither is established. This is recorded as a real, live, undecided question, not resolved by this investigation, and not something to assume answered until real synthesis output is observed.
part4_reassessment.4_model_diversity_vs_council_structure: UNCHANGED, restated explicitly per the mission's own instruction: this experiment, even fully repaired, may NOT claim to isolate 'council orchestration' from 'model diversity.' The only defensible claim available is the bounded one: 'the real Council package (diversity + selection + synthesis structure, taken together) versus a same-model, budget-matched self-consistency baseline.' Any report that speaks of 'orchestration' or 'architecture' in isolation from diversity, without this explicit caveat attached, overclaims.
part4_reassessment.5_is_the_budget_definition_still_correct: YES, unchanged and re-confirmed: identical call count + identical declared max_tokens per corresponding call is the primary definition; actual generated tokens, wall-clock, memory pressure, swap, and queue latency are all secondary measurements, explicitly never substituted for the primary definition anywhere in this investigation's own analysis.
